questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia for its weather and natural landscapes. I was very happy to stay in the state of Queensland, which is the gateway to all of the beautiful east coast, Great Barrier Reef and is subtropically warm all year.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ offers a great academic experience, while Australia itself offers unlimited travel and adventure opportunities both for nature and city lovers

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UQ does an awesome job  with providing any kind of information needed and are always proactive in supporting and being responsive to any inquiries

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UQ arranges a hole week of orientation with fun events both socially and academically. Besides that they offer both mental health support, academic support, housing support and personal issues support through the student service which is available both online and onsite

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UQ does a far better job than KU in regard of caring for their students and being responsive and helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: UQ offers both colleges (similar to Danish kollektiver) and individual student living meaning own room with private bathroom. I stayed at Kev Carmody House whic has amazing facilities, look it up if interested - rooms get booked out quickly.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At the colleges all daily meals are included in the rent and cooked for the residents. At Kev Carmody house which is currently the only independent living (2023) you have access to gourmet kitchen shared facilities and cook your own meals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It’s amazingly convenient but you do also tend to stay in the little campus bubble a lot this way, forgetting to go out and about and it’s a tad bit expensive compared to finding an of campus share house with some mates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ’s system is very logical and guides you through each step of the process

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I must say I forgot besides the fact that it was smooth and painless

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UQ offer online guiding session via zoom to help international students through the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: UQ was happy to let me into any courses I wished for what so ever, but KU has some rigid rules limiting the options for master students. However UQ was very helpful in assisting me in finding other courses I was happy with choosing instead

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Communicate with UQ try are so lovely and re-motivates you to make the exchange happen whenever KU demotivates you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is slightly lower than that of Denmark, however language barriers and adjusting to a foreign educational system can cause some challenges to deal with instead. Totally worth it tho and great learning experience on seeing tho Mhh a from a different perspective than the Danish one

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Far more hands on and career geared than the lecture heavy style of humanities in DK

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Digital heritage, academic English and thesis writing for international students, museum management, visitor management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visitor management was the most engaging course I’ve ever taken. The professors do a great job making the lectures entertaining, useful and interactive always filled with practical exercises and themes to dress up as or bring cultural food for. The other happy surprise was digital heritage which was very up to date and gave invaluable applicable skills for photogrammetry, object handling, coding, podcast producing and more

questions.answer: Living in Brisbane is rather expensive for student accom. The food is slightly cheaper than in Denmark but eating out is the same.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: See the above

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ has 200+ clubs for social activities of almost any kind u can imagine, from sports to arts to science to mediation etc. besides that UQ arranges loads of events throughout the semester

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Oh see the above :)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since student accom also arranges events I ended up travelling more with them, but definitely go to the free breakfast and UQ festivals plus o week - this is where to make a lot of friends and ppl are really open to chatting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try and get your uni work done during the week (doable) and then go on day trips or if u have a car longer trips in nature during weekends. I recommend Tallebudgera Creek on the Gold Coast and Noosa on the Sunshine Coast. For holidays snorkel the southern Great Barrier Reef at lady Musgrave island. Straddle is worth a daytrip as well

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australia has for the most part a western culture similar to the American one. They are far more chatty but on a rather superficial level tho they are very welcoming and helpful, but asking how are you going is just a greeting and not that sincere

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Chat to anyone - it will be so easy to make friends this way because everyone on campus is in a similar situation to yours

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People don’t raise there hands when they speak in class - you just speak out loud whenever. The constant small talk with the Australians is something that Mig be challenging for a Scandinavian to keep up with, the fact that they never dive into deep convos. Conservative politics and values from the older generations.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness and openness to make new friends

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it :) Brush up on your written and spoken English. Have fun with it, don’t worry too much about the grades

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun with it, take whatever you can use from the classes and don’t worry too much besides that. You’re probably in the country more for the cultural experience than the academic one anyways.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling around the country, making friends with Australians to get an insight into the authentic Australian life. Experiencing how easy it is to make friends in other countries than Denmark where we tend to be more cold and closed.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to adjust to the more laid back time perception and less timeliness when it comes to making appointments with Aussie friends, they might also cancel last minute.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was so worth it! Definitely go if you can and apply for grants at home beforehand - it takes you a long way

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
